Source Library · a map of the catalogue

What the library holds on ritual, tradition by tradition

Every primary source on liturgy, sacrifice, initiation, magic, funerary and calendar rite, monastic rule and ceremonial that Source Library holds, found by searching the full catalogue of 113,276 records and grouped into eight traditions. Each entry links to the book; the dot beside it says whether a reader can open it today.

How to read it. "Readable" means the book is public and at least nine pages in ten are translated. "Partly" means public with some of its text transcribed or translated. "Held, not yet public" means the library has the book but it cannot be opened yet, most often a library scan that has not been transcribed: 2,200 of the 5,299 cited books. Those entries are not links. The dots were checked against the catalogue on 18 Oct 2026.

Method. Eight surveys ran in parallel over a local dump of the catalogue taken at 09:33 on 9 September 2026, each with a checklist of canonical works and the instruction to search in the sources' own vocabulary (Latin, German, French, Wylie, pinyin, transliterations). Every one of the 5,299 cited book ids was checked against the dump before it became a link; 14 hand-typed slips were corrected. Gap lists name public-domain sources but flag every identifier the surveyor could not verify.

c. 2400 BCE – 1800 CE

Egypt, Mesopotamia & the Hebrew tradition

493 books cited253 readable101 partly134 held, not public121,303 pages held

Shape of the holdings

  1. Egypt is a Book-of-the-Dead library, not a ritual library: BoD is deep (Budge ×6, Lepsius, Naville, Greenfield, Ani facsimile, 9 Met papyri, ~425 artwork records) and the hymns/wisdom papyri are held as TLA-derived originals, but the actual ritual corpus — Pyramid/Coffin Texts, Opening of the Mouth, daily temple ritual, embalming, Bremner-Rhind, Breathings, Gates/Caverns/Litany, Dendera/Edfu, execration texts — is entirely absent; magic is Greek/Demotic only (PGM ×3, Griffith-Thompson).
  2. Mesopotamia is strong on Sumerian liturgy and Enuma Elish, absent on Akkadian exorcism: ~355 ETCSL compositions (temple hymns, city laments, Inana cycle, Gudea, royal prayers) plus Langdon ×6, King, Thureau-Dangin Rituels accadiens (the one Akitu source), Thompson Devils I, Montgomery bowls, Lidzbarski Mandaean — but no Maqlû, Šurpu, Namburbi, Zimmern, Jensen, Fossey, King Magic; Anatolia and Ugarit are zero; Phoenician only via Cooke (h) and Cory.
  3. Hebrew/Jewish is manuscript-rich but print-thin: Rylands/Gaster supplies ~40 liturgical MSS across Ashkenazi, French, Persian, Yemenite, Corfu, Indian, Karaite and Samaritan rites, 9 Haggadot, ~60 amulets, Raziel, Sword of Moses, Hekhalot MSS, a Yom Kippur Avodah, Shaʿar ha-Kavvanot, Tikkunei Zohar — but no Shulchan Aruch OḤ, Kol Bo, Manhig, Vitry, Amram, Saadia, Abudarham, Pri Etz Ḥayyim, Siddur ha-Ari, Selichot/Kinot/Hoshanot editions, Sefer ha-Razim, Shimmush Tehillim, Sefer Ḥasidim.
  4. Christian-Hebraist reception is the best-covered tier: Spencer, Vitringa ×2, Buxtorf Synagoga (Latin), Picart complete, Eisenmenger, Cunaeus, Selden ×3, Lightfoot Horae, Saubert, Hospinian, Jonston, Ricius, Leon's Temple, plus ~40 VD17 dissertations on individual rites (scapegoat, keriah, ḥalitzah, lustration, Passover reclining, mourning) — missing Modena, Bodenschatz, Outram, Reland, Goodwin, Braun, Lightfoot Temple Service, Maimonides De sacrificiis, Ugolini; and ~60% of what is held is h with 0–25 pages OCR'd.
  5. Readability: the Egyptian and Sumerian tiers are almost all V and fully translated, and the Rylands/Gaster MSS are mostly V and OCR'd; the Latin dissertation layer and the 1900s–1970s Assyriological/Egyptological editions (Breasted II–V, Barton, Thureau-Dangin SAKI, Langdon Penitential Psalms, Lambert, Hallo, Budge Egyptian Magic, Shaʿar ha-Kavvanot, Otzerot Ḥayyim) are held-not-read — OCR passes on those are cheaper wins than new imports.
Full survey, work by work

Source: local dump scratchpad/wisdom/books.jsonl (113K books), searched 2026-09-09 with scratchpad/ritual/grep.mjs (title/author/collection/summary regex). Not verified against Mongo.

Line format: - <work> — <id> | <title> | <author> | <lang> | <year> | V/h | count/ocr/translated Tags: [orig] original-language source (papyrus, tablet, MS, Hebrew print); [ed] scholarly edition (original text + apparatus); [tr] translation; [study] modern secondary work; [recep] early-modern Christian-Hebraist / antiquarian. h with 0/0 OCR = held (bulk import) but not yet readable. URL: sourcelibrary.org/book/

Shape of the holdings

  1. Strong: Neoplatonic theurgy (Iamblichus De mysteriis in 35 records across every Ficino printing plus Gale, Parthey, Taylor, Hopfner; Porphyry; Proclus; Psellus; Chaldean Oracles via Patrizi/Opsopoeus/Stanley/Kroll/Mead), Orphica (MSS, Aldine, Hermann, Abel, Kern, Taylor), Mithras (Cumont complete, Dieterich), Hermetica (deep), and the Gnostic/Mandaean/church-order corpus (Pistis Sophia ×6, Bruce Codex ×2, Didache ×3, Apostolic Constitutions/Didascalia ×3, Lidzbarski complete, Norberg).
  2. Solid but original-language-only: the Roman literary sources — Cicero's religious treatises, Livy, Macrobius, Gellius, Festus, Servius, Cato/Varro are present in early Latin editions and mostly translated; Ovid Fasti exists only as 8 Latin editions (2 visible) with no modern translation; Plutarch's ritual essays are in Bernardakis and Loeb, but the two key Loebs (IV–V) are hidden.
  3. Thin: the 19th/20th-century Religionswissenschaft layer is nearly absent — no Lobeck, Rohde, Harrison, Nilsson, Foucart, Marquardt, Preller, Fowler, Boissier; only Wissowa, Cumont, Reitzenstein, Creuzer, Farnell (1 vol) and Frazer (1 vol) represent it. The Renaissance antiquarians (Rosinus, Brisson, Saubert, Giraldi, Pignoria, Cartari, Conti, Beuther) are held but almost all hidden with 0–25 pp OCR.
  4. Papyri/defixiones: Preisendanz I, Audollent, Parthey, Griffith–Thompson, Dieterich Abraxas and McCown are here; missing are the pre-Preisendanz editions (Wessely, Kenyon I, Leemans, Goodwin), all of Wünsch, Heim, and the amulet literature. The 13 Berlin PGM records are catalogue stubs with no pages.
  5. Norse/Celtic: small but well chosen (Resen Edda, Rask, Saxo, Adam of Bremen, Ibn Fadlan, Olaus Magnus, Grimm, Worm, Arnkiel, Davies, Toland, Carmina Gadelica) — the primary sources are here; the German comparative scholarship (Mannhardt Feldkulte, Golther, Simrock, Bugge, Keysler, Bartholin) is not.

  2. STRONG but unread (held hidden, 0–25 pp OCR — the cheapest expansion of the map): the Upper-Rhine incunable series of missals/breviaries/graduals (Basel, Konstanz, Geneva, Lausanne, Strasbourg, Naumburg, Bursfeld, Dominican, Teutonic), the Rylands "Latin MS" liturgica (Sarum Missal, Colonna Missals, Exultet Roll, antiphoners, Horae), the Rule of St Benedict (three prints + Turrecremata + Smaragdus MS, none readable), Guigo's Carthusian Statuta, Hittorp 1568 (which contains Amalarius, Rabanus, Walafrid, Beleth etc. in one volume), Mabillon Museum Italicum II (Ordines Romani), Bona, Gavanti, Pamelius, Casali, Duranti, Cassander, the ~230-title 16th-c. Latin Eucharistic controversy, the Anhalt baptismal-exorcism pamphlet cluster, and the 1793 Slavonic Dobrotolyubie.
  3. THIN: pontificals and episcopal ceremonial (fragments), post-Tridentine diocesan missals outside Switzerland, the Byzantine liturgies themselves (only Anglican 19th-c. editions), hesychast core texts (one Philokalia volume), Armenian/Coptic/Slavonic service books (one each or none), monastic customaries, Protestant liturgical formularies proper (one BCP, one Dutch baptism form, one Low-German church order), festival/entry books, confraternity statutes.
  4. ABSENT: Caeremoniale episcoporum 1600 and Caeremoniale Romanum 1516, Pontificale Romanum in full, Muratori/Tommasi/Gerbert/Martène/Le Brun/Benedict XIV/Assemani/Goar, Mozarabic and Ambrosian missals, Slavonic Sluzhebnik/Trebnik, Horologion/Triodion/Menaion/Typikon, Symeon of Thessalonica, Cabasilas, Codex regularum (Holstenius) and every early rule except Benedict/Augustine, Cluniac/Cistercian customaries, Jesuit Constitutions, all coronation ordines (Liber Regalis, Godefroy, Menin, Wahl- und Krönungsdiarien), royal touch, liturgical drama and Passion plays, everything German by Luther/Zwingli/Bucer on worship, Calvin's Forme des prières, all BCPs but 1662, Knox in English, Westminster Directory, Wesley, Kirchenordnungen, metrical psalters, 19th-c. Anglican ritualism.
  5. Net: the library's Christian-ritual strength is late-medieval and early-modern Latin devotional/ritual PRACTICE (Hours, chant MSS, missals, exorcism, Ars moriendi, Trent) and the polemics around it; the scholarly-liturgiological layer (Maurists, Muratori, HBS/Surtees, Duchesne–Cabrol) and the non-Latin service books (Byzantine, Slavonic, Reformation vernaculars) are the two big holes.

Full survey, work by work

Scope: liturgy, sacraments, monastic rules, exorcism, coronation and civic ceremonial, Eastern rites and hesychasm, Reformation liturgies, and the scholarship of liturgy. Source: local JSONL dump of all ~113K book records (scratchpad/wisdom/books.jsonl) via scratchpad/ritual/grep.mjs; no Mongo queries. Six groups, each surveyed separately; per-group GAPS and Shape sections are kept in place, and a consolidated summary is at the end.

Line format everywhere: - <work> — <id> | <title> | <author> | <lang> | <year> | V/h | count/ocr/translated [ORIG|TRANS|STUDY]. Book URL = sourcelibrary.org/book/. V = visible, h = hidden. Hidden rows with 0 OCR are bulk library imports (BSB/e-rara/Basel/John Rylands "Latin MS", Penn "Catholic Church" MSS) — HELD but not readable; visible + translated = readable.

Shape of the holdings

  1. Strong: Tibetan/Bhutanese practitioner ritual (1,286 fully translated liturgical texts across six monastic collections, plus two Kangyurs with ~40 tantra volumes, a 38-vol Nyingma Gyubum, and 400 BDRC volumes waiting on OCR) — this is where the library's "map of ritual" is deepest; Kashmiri Śāradā domestic ritual (~1,490 MSS, ~300 ritual manuals, held but 0 OCR); Woodroffe-era Śākta tantra and Kashmir Śaiva (Tantrāloka complete and readable; Somaśambhupaddhati and Kriyāsamuccaya are real prizes); the complete Indian SBE run (all 33 vols, Satapatha and Gṛhya complete); graha-śānti manuals (12 readable).
  2. Adequate: Ṛgveda (Müller 1–5 + Griffith), Atharvaveda (Bloomfield, Whitney, Pandit 3/5), Dharmaśāstra in translation (Manu, Viṣṇu, Āpastamba/Gautama, Nārada), Pali Vinaya (SBE 13/17 readable, 20 hidden) and Pali canon, Purāṇas in Sanskrit (Agni, Garuḍa, Liṅga, Brahma, Skanda), Haṭha-yoga triad, Bardo Thödol (three Tibetan recensions + Evans-Wentz), Balinese ritual lontar (present, 0 OCR).
  3. Thin: Śrauta ritual proper — Caland's Agniṣṭoma is the only full description; no Śrauta-sūtra text except a fragment of Mānava; no Brāhmaṇa in Sanskrit besides a 1-page Śatapatha stub; Sāma/Yajur almost bare; Gṛhya in Sanskrit only Gobhila and Hiraṇyakeśin; Buddhist Sanskrit tantra (one Kriyāsamuccaya, no Sādhanamālā/Guhyasamāja); Theravada ritual (one Burmese prayer book; no paritta, no Kammavācā); Jain and Sikh ritual (canon and Granth present, no pūjā/pratikramaṇa/rahit); Bon (one Dzogchen cycle, no rites).
  4. Absent: the whole German śrauta-philology shelf (Hillebrandt, Schwab, Weber Rājasūya, Caland Zauberritual, Bloomfield Kauśika), the classic European ethnography of Hindu rites (Colebrooke, Ward, Dubois, Stevenson, Wilson Sects, Ziegenbalg, Roger, Sonnerat, Bernier, Tavernier), Āgama/Pāñcarātra/Vaikhānasa temple ritual, Mīmāṃsā sūtras with Śabara, Ceylon/Burma/Siam monastic ethnography (Hardy, Upham, Copleston, Bowring), Tengyur, and the Tibetological reception (Georgi, Huc, Köppen, Grünwedel Mythologie).
  5. Operational note: the two largest ritual corpora (Śāradā MSS, BDRC) are held-but-invisible; readers currently see Bhutan and the Woodroffe/KSTS prints. Item-level indexing of the 40 Kangyur rGyud volumes and OCR of the ~300 Śāradā ritual manuals would change the map more than any acquisition.

Shape of the holdings

  1. Strong, original-language, unreadable: the Confucian ritual canon is held in extraordinary depth — Zhouli, Yili, Liji each in 15–20 commentary editions (Zheng Xuan zhushu, Qianlong yishu, Song–Qing exegesis), plus 五禮通考 (180 vols), 讀禮通考, 三禮圖, Jiali, Shuyi, 泰泉鄉禮 — but this entire 6a3c… layer is Chinese-only, 25-page OCR samples, 0 pages translated; the readable Confucian ritual layer is Legge SBE 27–28, Couvreur's Li Ki, Legge's Classics, Dubs's Xunzi and de Groot's six volumes.
  2. Strong and readable: de Groot (6 vols), Doré (4 of 15 vols), Kircher, Ricci/Trigault, Du Halde, Confucius Sinarum Philosophus, the neidan cluster (Cantong qi ×8, Xingming guizhi, Zhen'gao, Baopuzi, Bai Yuchan), Korean uigwe ×3 + Ŭirye munhae + Pure Land repentance liturgy, Kojiki/Nihongi/Man'yōshū originals with Aston, the Kanze utaibon (30 vols) and Zeami.
  3. Thin: Daoist liturgy proper — beyond two Daozang fascicles and catalogues there is no Lingbao, Zhengyi, jiao/zhai, talisman, morality-book or Ganying pian text; Chinese Buddhist ritual — one monastic code (hidden), one dhāraṇī print, one mantra scroll, a few sutras, no repentance/Shuilu/Yulanpen liturgy and no Beal/Edkins/Johnston; Japanese Buddhism — Dōgen and Ennin held only as unread woodblocks, nothing for Kūkai/Shingon, Hōnen/Shinran, Nichiren or Shugendō.
  4. Held-but-dark (0 OCR, high value, cheap to fix): Engishiki + Engishiki norito, Kogo shūi, Sendai kuji hongi, Izumo fudoki, Motoori Kojiki-den, Revon's Anciens rituels, Baizhang qinggui 1442, Lüzu quanshu, Le Favre's Rites acta 1700, Thomas's Brevis relatio 1701, Innocentia victrix 1671, Pallas's Mongolische Völkerschaften, Rhodes's Tonkin history, Hulbert's Passing of Korea, Legge's SBE 3 and 39–40 duplicates.
  5. Absent: every dynastic ritual code, Confucian-temple and Heaven-altar liturgy, oracle bones, the Wilhelm/Régis Yijing, Lettres édifiantes and Amiot's Mémoires (0 volumes of either), the Rites Controversy's major printed treatises (Longobardi, Navarrete, Le Comte, Le Gobien, Leibniz), Satow/Florenz norito, all tea-ceremony and bushidō classics, Manchu shamanic ritual, Korean state rites (Gukjo oryeui), and everything Vietnamese beyond Rhodes and one gazetteer.
Full survey, work by work

Surveyed 2026-09-09 against the local dump (scratchpad/wisdom/books.jsonl, 113,276 records). Every title field was searched in Chinese/Japanese/Korean script, pinyin, Wade-Giles, romaji and the standard European forms; author searches for the named sinologists/japanologists were run separately. Multi-volume bulk imports are collapsed to one line per work with [N vols] and summed page counts.

Line format: - <work> — <id> | <title> | <author> | <lang> | <year> | V/h | count/ocr/translated — build links as https://sourcelibrary.org/book/<id>. Tags: [orig] original-language source, [trans] translation, [study] modern/European study or travel account, [stub] catalogue record with 0 pages (held as a record only).

Two import families dominate the Chinese side and need to be read correctly:

  • 6a3c… ids = the big Siku quanshu-style commentary import (2026). Visible, Chinese only, OCR sampled at ~25 pages per volume, 0 translated. Held and browsable as images, not yet readable in English.
  • 69bd0…/69b63f…/69b635… ids = hidden records with 0 OCR (NDL-style Japanese woodblocks, and library catalogue stubs). Held, not readable.

Shape of the holdings

  1. Strong: Qur'an as object (Hijazi to Ruzbihan, first printed Arabic 1694, Marracci, Du Ryer, Sale, Rodwell, Palmer); Zoroastrian text-editions (Anquetil to Geldner, all SBE Avesta/Pahlavi volumes, a Yasna liturgical MS, Modi's ceremonies manual, Hyde 1700, Persian Zoroastrian MSS incl. Ṣad dar); Arabic magic core (Būnī ×4, two Arabic Ghāyat al-ḥakīm, Kitāb al-Bulhān, an Arabic raml treatise); Rumi/Ibn ʿArabī/Ghazali/Qushayrī/Hujwīrī/Sarrāj in original languages; West African and Zulu ethnography (Callaway, Ellis ×4, Kingsley, Nassau, Rattray, Talbot, Junod, Frobenius, Dennett); Druze (Rasāʾil al-ḥikma + de Sacy); Chwolsohn on the Sabians; Doutté and Westermarck on Maghribi ritual.
  2. Unexpected strength: the Leiden Or. Indonesian manuscripts and the Javanese "WM ID" pesantren collection form a real 19th-c. Southeast-Asian ritual library — ~15 duʿāʾ books, wird/awrād, 8 Rifāʿī rātib/dhikr booklets, mawlid fragments, khutba collection, salat and fasting fiqh, 5 copies of Nawawī's Minhāj, Sammāniyya dhikr method, Shaṭṭārī/Qādirī silsilas — but most WM ID items are hidden with 0 OCR, and Arabic-script OCR is the gate.
  3. Thin: hadith (one Bukhārī, one Muslim fragment, one Kāfī); fiqh of worship outside Ghazālī and the Javanese MSS (no Hidāya, Bidāya, Qayrawānī, Shiʿi fiqh); Ottoman/Persian/Mughal court ritual (Evliya held but barely OCR'd; Āʾīn-i Akbarī partial; Dabistān only in Persian MSS); Sufi orders as institutions (nothing on Depont-Coppolani/Rinn/Brown; no ʿAwārif, no Aflākī); European traveller-reporters of ritual (only Niebuhr, Lane, Kaempfer, Leo Africanus, Montagu); Ethiopia (one magic MS, Kebra Nagast, Ludolf un-OCR'd); Manichaean (Boyce, Allberry).
  4. Absent: hajj literature (no Burton, Burckhardt Arabia, Snouck, Ibn Jubayr, manāsik); the great Sunni prayer books (Dalāʾil al-khayrāt, Burda, Adhkār); Shiʿi ritual (no Ṣaḥīfa, Nahj, taʿziya — no Pelly/Chodzko); Nusayri, Ibadi, Ismaili texts; d'Ohsson; Zār/Gnawa; dream books; Falasha; Ifa/Candomblé/Santería/Obeah studies (only Owen's Voodoo Tales and Moreau de Saint-Méry); van Gennep, Durkheim Formes, Marett, Lagrange.
  5. Readability caveat: the six Bibliander Latin Qur'ans, Sale 1734, Būnī's full Shams al-maʿārif (304 pp), Spiegel vol. 2, Bleeck, SBE 18/24, Ludolf, Maqrīzī, Ibn Baṭṭūṭa and almost every Rylands Persian MS are held but have 0-50 pages OCR'd — on this map they count as "held, not readable"; the cheapest wins are OCR runs, not imports.

Shape of the holdings

  1. Strong: Mesoamerican primary sources — full Florentine Codex, 13 pictorial codices, Popol Vuh in manuscript plus first two printings, six Chilam Balam books, Landa (x3), Cogolludo, Sánchez de Aguilar, and the 84-book 6a9f new-world wave (Durán, Torquemada, Motolinía, Las Casas, Clavigero, Veytia, Boturini, Kingsborough). But the whole wave is hidden and 80/84 have zero OCR — held, not readable, and untagged (so mesoamerican/americas undercount by ~80).
  2. Strong but un-processed: Andes (Guaman Poma, Garcilaso, Acosta visible and translated; Cieza, Cobo, Arriaga, Sarmiento, Calancha, Molina/Pachacuti, Oré 1607 hidden), Baltic/Finnic (Kalevala 1835, Kalevipoeg, Einhorn x3, Mannhardt, Boecler — all visible), Picart (9 records, 8 visible, ~9,000 pages translated), and the 1690s-1730s superstition literature (Bekker x4, Le Brun, Van Dale, Buddeus).
  3. Thin: North America is only Americanist monographs (Mooney, Cushing, Matthews, Boas, Swanton, Densmore, Hale) — zero Jesuit Relations, zero Lafitau/Charlevoix, zero BAE series; Oceania is Grey (x4), Cook I, Codrington, Spencer & Gillen and Hawaiian material — no Ellis, Best, Howitt, Haddon; Siberia is early-modern travel (Scheffer x3 hidden, Strahlenberg, Pallas hidden, Krasheninnikov) with no 19th-20th c. shamanism ethnography.
  4. Absent: every Christian doctrina/confesionario in an indigenous American language except Eliot's Bible and Oré; Ruiz de Alarcón/Serna; Pérez Bocanegra; Mapuche/Guaraní ritual beyond Montoya's lexicon; the Caribbean chroniclers; Blair & Robertson; the British/German folklore canon after Brand (Mannhardt, Wuttke, Hone, Chambers, Dyer, Gomme, Sébillot, Van Gennep, Leland); and the core of ritual theory (Frazer beyond GB1 vol. 1, Tylor vol. II, Lang, Hubert & Mauss, Durkheim's Formes, Harrison, Marett, Van Gennep, Otto, Freud Totem).
  5. Housekeeping: duplicates to merge — Dresden Codex (2), Landa/Brasseur (3), Popol Vuh Brasseur (3), Grey Polynesian Mythology (4), Piso (2), Westervelt Historical Legends (2), Boemus (3), Scheffer (3), Chumayel/Gordon (2); seven 0-page stubs to delete or merge (69b636 Florentine, 69b636 and 69b636 Popol Vuh, 69b636 Chimalpopoca, 69b636 Tizimin, 69b636 Huarochirí, 69b636 Cantares); two Picart records mislabelled "Latin".
